title: The cash leak
brief: Overdue invoices went from EUR 26k to EUR 1.0M in six months. Cash is tight before the winter season.
assumption: The CFO's theory: all our customers pay slower now, so we need stricter payment terms for everyone.
question: Is it really everyone? Find who is behind the rise and what we should do this week.

hints.text: Only unpaid invoices matter. Group the overdue ones by customer: how concentrated is it?
Look at the top name in A_SalesOrder too. Is anything still waiting to ship to them?

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.

title: The plan gap
brief: Revenue is at 97.2% of plan with the fiscal year closed. The board wants one region to blame.
assumption: The sales board blames the Nordics, where a large dealer was just blocked by the credit check.
question: Which region really cost us the plan, since when, and why?

hints.text: Compare revenue per SalesRegion with ZI_SalesPlan. Which region is furthest away in %?
Plot that region month by month, then split it by customer. Who stopped ordering?

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.

title: Christmas at risk
brief: Christmas orders peak in six weeks. Hamburg builds all Urban and Trail e-bikes.
assumption: Production says aluminium frames are the bottleneck, because a large frame PO is still open.
question: Can Hamburg build bikes through November? If not, which part stops the line, when, and what can we do?

hints.text: DaysOfCover in A_MaterialStock tells you how long each component lasts at plant 1010.
Compare on-time delivery per supplier over the year. Is there a second source for the critical part?

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.

title: The full warehouse
brief: Inventory is worth EUR 18.4M vs. a EUR 17.5M target. Every extra euro in stock is cash we cannot use.
assumption: The CFO wants Hamburg, our biggest warehouse, to cut its stock by 10%.
question: Where is the excess stock really, what is it, and why did it build up?

hints.text: Compare each plant against its own StockTargetValue, not against the others.
What kind of product (ProductType) fills that plant, and since which month has it grown?

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.

title: The recycling claim
deadline: Annual report goes to print on Monday
brief: The annual report draft says: "Every Northwind plant recycles at least 90% of its waste."
assumption: Communications thinks it's true, because the group average is 91.1%.
question: Is the sentence true for every plant? If not, which plant, and how far below 90% is it?

hints.text: Show every plant next to a 90% target, so the reader sees at once which one is below it.

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.

title: The renewable gap
brief: Only 68.6% of the electricity we use is renewable. The target is 75%.
assumption: The sustainability team thinks the new solar roof in Hamburg isn't working well.
question: Which plant keeps us below 75%, and when will that change?

hints.text: Renewable share per plant = RenewableElectricityMWh ÷ ElectricityMWh. Use .ratio().
Look at that plant in ZI_SustainabilityInitiative: which project fixes it, and when does it go live?

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.

title: The CO2 overshoot
brief: This year the plants emitted 12,480 t of CO2e. The budget was 11,500 t.
assumption: The board thinks the new wheel line in Porto caused it.
question: Which plant caused the overshoot, since which month, and what should the board decide?

hints.text: Compare each plant's CO2eTonnes with its own BudgetCO2eTonnes.
Show that plant month by month next to its budget. What changes in April? Check its initiatives.

deliverable: One page: your finding in one sentence, one or two charts that prove it, and one action.
